description: Non-functional requirements for the Faster Payment Initiation journey. All requirements are derived from regulatory obligations (PSRs 2017, OFSI regulations, PSR PS23/3), Pay.UK/Vocalink FPS scheme rules, FCA operational resilience obligations (SS1/21), and the bank's internal payment service SLAs.

nfrs.requirement: Happy-path payment initiation (from SCA completion to confirmation screen render) must complete in < 15 seconds in the 95th percentile.
nfrs.measurement_point: From timestamp on SVC-001 PaymentIntentCreated event to timestamp on SVC-017 rendering confirmation screen (GET /payments/{id} returning status = completed)
nfrs.regulatory_basis: PSRs 2017 Regulation 86 — payment service providers must execute payment orders promptly. FCA Consumer Duty — payment services must deliver good outcomes for customers including speed expectations consistent with market norms.

nfrs.requirement: SVC-051 (Sanctions Screening Service) must return a screening result within 3,000ms for 99th percentile of requests.
nfrs.measurement_point: From SVC-051 receiving the screen request payload to returning the screening result
nfrs.regulatory_basis: GOV-005-R02 — OFSI real-time screening obligation. Batch-end screening is non-compliant; screening must occur before transaction is processed.
nfrs.failure_mode: If SVC-051 exceeds 3,000ms, SVC-001 must apply a conservative block (fail closed): PaymentIntent transitions to status = sanctions_timeout, MLRO is notified, and customer receives a generic processing delay message.

nfrs.requirement: SVC-013 (Fraud Detection) must return a fraud score within 500ms for 99th percentile of requests.
nfrs.measurement_point: From SVC-013 receiving the FraudScore request (via PaymentIntentCreated event) to publishing FraudScoreCompleted event
nfrs.regulatory_basis: No direct statutory latency obligation; requirement is derived from the end-to-end < 15 second target (NFR-JRN002-001) and competitive market expectation (Monzo, Starling: real-time fraud decisioning without perceptible delay).
nfrs.failure_mode: If SVC-013 fails to respond within 500ms timeout, SVC-001 must apply a conservative hold: PaymentIntent transitions to status = fraud_review_timeout; payment is queued for Fraud Analyst (PER-054) manual review. Customer notified of processing delay.

nfrs.requirement: All Faster Payments submitted to Pay.UK/Vocalink via SVC-009 must achieve D+0 same-day settlement (intraday settlement cycle).
nfrs.target: D+0 settlement for all payments submitted before the FPS scheme cutoff window. Payments accepted by Vocalink are typically credited to beneficiary within 2 hours and often within seconds.
nfrs.scheme_constraints: FPS operates 24/7/365 with near-continuous availability. Vocalink SLA to Pay.UK participants is 99.9% availability.
nfrs.regulatory_basis: PSRs 2017 Regulation 86 — end-of-next-business-day execution for domestic credit transfers. FPS exceeds this requirement with same-day settlement. Pay.UK FPS Participation Rules.

nfrs.requirement: The payment initiation service (SVC-001 payments endpoint and SVC-009 FPS execution) must achieve 99.99% availability, measured monthly.
nfrs.target: 99.99% monthly availability (< 4.38 minutes downtime per month)
nfrs.measurement: Uptime measured at the SVC-001 POST /payments endpoint and GET /payments/{id} endpoint. Planned maintenance windows must occur outside 08:00–22:00 on business days.
nfrs.regulatory_basis: FCA Operational Resilience SS1/21 — payment services are designated an 'important business service'. The board must set an impact tolerance (maximum tolerable disruption). FCA supervisory expectation: tolerance of 0 minutes for payment initiation outages during business hours. PSR PS23/3 — APP fraud reimbursement obligation implies payments must be available to initiate.
nfrs.impact_tolerance: 0 minutes disruption tolerated during core payment hours (08:00–22:00 daily). Out-of-hours: 30 minutes maximum.

nfrs.requirement: Where a PER-001 submits an APP fraud reimbursement claim, the bank must complete the reimbursement decisioning process and pay eligible claimants within 5 business days of the claim being submitted.
nfrs.target: 100% of eligible claims reimbursed within 5 business days
exceptions: Stop-the-clock provisions apply if: (a) the bank reasonably suspects the customer acted fraudulently; (b) the bank requires further information and has notified the customer; (c) the customer is under gross negligence investigation.
nfrs.audit_requirement: Every claim decision (approve, partial approve, decline) must be recorded in the immutable audit log (SVC-111) with decision rationale, amount, and processing timestamps.
nfrs.regulatory_basis: GOV-003-R01 — PSR PS23/3 APP Fraud Mandatory Reimbursement (in force 7 October 2024).

nfrs.requirement: Confirmation of Payee checks must be performed on 100% of outbound FPS payments before the PaymentIntent is created. No blanket exemptions permitted.
nfrs.target: 100% CoP coverage rate on all FPS payment instructions
nfrs.reporting: CoP coverage rate reported to PSR annually per GOV-003-R02 disclosure obligation.
nfrs.regulatory_basis: GOV-003-R02 — PSR Specific Direction 17 (SD17); PSR Group 2 mandatory from October 2024.

nfrs.requirement: Every payment instruction must be protected by Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) with dynamic linking. The SCA must bind to the specific payee sort code, account number, and payment amount. SCA is completed at the channel layer before POST /payments is called.
nfrs.target: 100% of payment instructions SCA-authenticated with dynamic linking
nfrs.regulatory_basis: PSRs 2017 Regulation 71 (strong customer authentication) and Regulation 100 (dynamic linking for credit transfers). EBA/FCA SCA technical standards.

nfrs.requirement: All PaymentIntent records, screening results, fraud scores, and payment execution records must be immutably logged to SVC-111 (WORM audit pipeline) and retained for 5 years minimum.
nfrs.target: 100% of payment events written to SVC-111 WORM pipeline within 500ms of publication
nfrs.retention_period: 5 years minimum (GOV-005-R02 — OFSI screening records); FCA BCOBS recommends 7 years for retail account records
nfrs.regulatory_basis: GOV-005-R02 (OFSI sanctions log retention); GOV-003-R01 (APP fraud reimbursement claims audit trail); MLR 2017 Regulation 40.

nfrs.requirement: The payment initiation service must support a minimum throughput of 500 concurrent payment initiations per second during peak periods, without degradation in P95 latency.
nfrs.target: 500 TPS sustained; 1,000 TPS burst (Black Friday, bank holiday eve peaks)
nfrs.rationale: UK FPS processed 5 billion transactions in 2024 (~158 per second average). Peak-to-average ratio for UK retail payments is approximately 6:1 intraday. The bank's estimated market share implies peak loads of 500 TPS. Headroom of 2x for burst scenarios.

nfrs.requirement: The payment initiation service must fail safely. If SVC-051 or SVC-013 are unavailable, the system must default to a conservative block (not a permissive pass-through) and queue payments for manual review.
nfrs.target: Fail-closed on SVC-051 (sanctions) unavailability. Fail-closed on SVC-013 (fraud) unavailability with auto-hold queue.
nfrs.rationale: Allowing payments through without sanctions screening would violate OFSI real-time screening obligations (GOV-005-R02). A sanctions-screening bypass during a service outage creates direct regulatory and criminal liability.
nfrs.circuit_breaker_policy: SVC-001 implements a circuit breaker for SVC-051. After 3 consecutive timeouts, the breaker opens and all new PaymentIntents are placed in status = sanctions_timeout_hold. MLRO is alerted. Breaker resets after SVC-051 health check passes.
